Work in motion

Know who is doing what, and where it stands.

Operations turns objectives into assignments and follows each team from briefing through return. Team status and task status stay distinct, so supervisors can see both capacity and progress.

One incident record

Assignments connect the sections.

Operations receives a plan, gives it to a team, and returns the result to the shared incident picture.

Assignment lifecycle

From tasking to closeout.

Every step keeps the responsible team, supervisor, location, and operational record attached to the work.

  1. 01Prepare

    Define the assignment, map area, hazards, and expected result.

  2. 02Brief

    Give the team its task and confirm the personnel and resources assigned.

  3. 03Track

    Follow status, location, field narrative, and changes in conditions.

  4. 04Close

    Record the result, team return, and anything that becomes new work.

Two connected boards

Capacity and progress are different questions.

Teams

Availability, staffing, movement, rest, and out-of-service conditions describe what a resource can do next.

Tasks

Planned, assigned, active, and completed work describes what has happened to an assignment.

Resource detail

The team is more than a callsign.

Open a team to review its personnel, aircrew where applicable, equipment, vehicles, aircraft, and task, status, unit, or ICS-214 activity logs. The available tabs follow the type of team.

  • Check composition and qualifications before assigning work.
  • Keep vehicles and equipment tied to the team using them.
  • Read the team’s activity in the same context as its assignments.
